mutant.description: Seven mutants submitted to the SAME Draft 2020-12 validator that produced the 4-of-4 PASS, run AFTER the final edits so they certify the DELIVERED bytes rather than an earlier draft. M1 trust block deleted. M2 floor violation on trust.key (scalar 'measured' over an 'inferred' sub-claim). M3 prose walked into a composes id (the ' -- ' pattern). M4 verdict.standing set to a non-enum value. M5 an unexpected additional property. M6 mutation_policy set to 'DESTRUCTIVE'. M7 THE FLOOR RULE ON A DIFFERENT ARM -- artifact.persistence.basis forced to 'measured' on W3-bzgw, the one card that genuinely carries inferred sub-claims, so the control is reachable from a DIFFERENT TRUTH than M2 rather than being the same mutation twice.
mutant.observed: 7 of 7 fired. Baseline re-confirmed under both Draft7 and Draft 2020-12: 4 of 4 VALID under each, so the PASS is not an artifact of validator choice. ⛔ AND THE CONTRACT CAUGHT TWO REAL DEFECTS OF MINE BEFORE DELIVERY, which is the point of running it against delivered bytes. (1) FLOOR RULE: THE CONTRACT REJECTED MY FIRST PASS AND IT WAS RIGHT. W3-bzgw shipped artifact.persistence with basis='measured' while form and mutation_policy were honestly marked 'inferred' -- because I have never seen the object that path would write, so I read its shape from the code instead. RESOLUTION: I DEMOTED THE SCALAR TO 'inferred' (the MIN over the map). I did NOT upgrade the two sub-claims to 'measured' to clear the gate -- that would have been falsifying a claim to satisfy a validator, which is the exact inversion of what the floor rule is for. The same demotion is why W3-bzgw's verdict discusses the floor rule explicitly on its face. (2) W3-dljc carried a composes id of 'portal (git submodule)', which the contract's id pattern forbids. Fixed by moving the parenthetical into the note, where prose belongs. ⚠ AND A CONTROL OF MY OWN THAT OVER-REPORTED: My own proactive id-pattern scan reported 4 remaining violations after the fix, all on subject.id. THEY WERE FALSE POSITIVES OF MY SCAN, not real violations: the pattern constraint applies to composes/invents ids, and my walker applied it to every key named 'id' including subject.id -- a control whose SUBJECT was the wrong field. Resolved against the validator itself rather than against my scan: all 4 cards validate, and W3-thav/W3-uuxp had already validated with the identical ':: PATH A -- ' subject id form before the fix. Recorded because a scan that over-reports looks like rigour and would have driven me to mangle four correct subject ids.
mutant.note: ⛔ M2 AND M7 ARE THE SAME RULE ON TWO DIFFERENT CARDS AND THAT IS DELIBERATE, per the control-set law that both arms must be reachable from different truths: M2 mutates a card whose sub-claims are all measured (the violation is injected), M7 mutates a card whose sub-claims are genuinely mixed (the violation is a real over-claim I could plausibly have shipped). M6 additionally CORROBORATES a finding I recorded independently on the W3-thav face -- v2's mutation_policy enum has no DESTRUCTIVE member -- which is why that card carries 'replaceable' as a declared floor-fit rather than a silent widening. I did NOT re-run 0.8.0_AE_CloudComp~X's forward_disposition self-disposal mutant: my cards omit forward_disposition entirely per W2-m-3, and re-running their mutant by their method would be REPETITION, not corroboration. I cite their finding as theirs.
